cells.tense: You're standing here with the pen in your hand, and what you pictured has come the whole way through into something you can stand in.
cells.ask: Notice what's already moving well, and let it carry you further into itself.
cells.core:
The thing you imagined has been felt all the way through, and it arrived. That's a different satisfaction from everything being right — it's that the imagining was complete, and you can rest inside it. Where things get weighed and set level, this is what going well actually looks like: you read what's fair quickly, you set the lines down, and neither the reading nor the line-setting grinds you down. Things sit square because you put them there, and you did it without strain.

The momentum underneath this isn't forced. What keeps it steady is that you're moving by what you actually feel, not by pushing. Follow what genuinely engages you, and the pace takes care of itself.
cells.sheetLine: You imagined it fully, it's here, and you're the one deciding what's fair.
cells.verb: arriving at the deep satisfaction of having fully imagined and fully felt something
cells.place: where what's out of proportion gets recalibrated until things sit fair again

cells.tense: You're leaning into a version of this that hasn't shown up yet, pre-correcting a balance that hasn't tipped.
cells.ask: Hold this like a garden — tend it, and don't pull the stems up to make them taller.
cells.core:
Fairness has stopped being something you work out and become something you get ahead of. You're measuring, adjusting, heading off an imbalance nobody's reported. The reaching is where the strain lives. At its working best, this looks like steady hands and unhurried care: you tend what's in front of you, the rest grows at its own rate, and none of that tending runs you flat.

What tends a thing without forcing it is attention that can just watch it grow. Give one adjustment less than you want to this week. Let what you've already built stand on its own for a while, and watch that it does.
cells.sheetLine: You're reaching to hold a balance that hasn't tipped yet.

cells.tense: You're standing on the far side of a door you already walked through, and the room you're in now is quiet.
cells.ask: Say what you already know, plainly, before you've built the case for saying it.
cells.core:
You're outside something you can see clearly from here. The satisfaction isn't something you're reaching for, and fair balance isn't something you're weighing. You watch both from a distance and you don't step back in. In good shape, your read of a situation just lands — no argument needed, no case assembled — and you act on it without having to convince yourself first. That ease is the part that's gone quiet.

The certainty is still in you. You don't have to push yourself toward the feeling. Name what you see, quietly, to one person, and the pull back into this follows on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly and you've stopped saying so.

cells.tense: You're already reading what's fair as you move through the day, and you describe the reading as if it happened without you.
cells.ask: Pick one call you made this week and own it out loud, once.
cells.core:
A sense of proportion is already shaping how you handle things — what you let go, what you correct, where you draw the line. You just tell it like the line drew itself. Running clean, this looks like quick, unhurried judgment: you sort what matters from what doesn't, the sorting isn't a fight with yourself, the calls hold up afterward, and you can trace each one back to a moment you decided it.

That sharpness is yours to claim. Refining it doesn't mean turning it on yourself. Notice which calls were already yours, and say so about one of them tonight.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one reading this — say so.
